classification.difficultyReason: Translate the percentages into forward branches, combine both routes to having a photo, and divide the limousine-and-photo probability by that total. This reverses the stated conditioning through the taught tree method.

inlines.text: At a Year 12 formal, 45% of the students travelled to the event in a hired limousine, while the remaining 55% were driven to the event by a parent.
Of the students who travelled in a hired limousine, 30% had a professional photo taken.
Of the students who were driven by a parent, 60% had a professional photo taken.
Given that a student had a professional photo taken, what is the probability that the student travelled to the event in a hired limousine?

answer.worked:
Let $L$ denote travel in a hired limousine and $F$ denote having a professional photo taken. The tree uses travel method first, followed by whether a photo was taken.

$$\begin{align*}P(L\cap F)&=0.45\times0.30\\&=0.135\\P(F)&=0.45\times0.30+0.55\times0.60\\&=0.465\\P(L\mid F)&=\frac{P(L\cap F)}{P(F)}\\&=\frac{0.45\times0.30}{(0.45\times0.30)+(0.55\times0.60)}\\&=\frac{9}{31}\end{align*}$$
